commentary: DCE iron ore futures hit a new low, with the market showing weak and volaƟle performance throughout the day. The most-traded contract I2501 ﬁnally closed at 734 yuan/mt, down 1.08% for the day. Traders showed moderate enthusiasm for selling; steel mills were cauƟously observing, with some planning tenders. Overall market transacƟon senƟment was average today. In Shandong, PB ﬁnes traded at 750-760 yuan/mt, down 10 yuan/mt WoW; in Tangshan, PB ﬁnes traded at 770-775 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt WoW. SMM reported global iron ore shipments at 31.87 million mt, down 2.8% WoW. Shipments from Australia were 16.75 million mt, down 7.3% WoW; shipments from Australia to China accounted for 82.1% of Australia's total shipments, down 4.8% WoW. Shipments from Brazil were 8.24 million mt, up 14% WoW; shipments from Brazil to China accounted for 56.4% of Brazil's total shipments, up 98.7% WoW. SMM reported China's iron ore arrivals at 26.11 million mt, up 33.22% WoW. Iron ore supply remains relaƟvely ample. However, blast furnace maintenance conƟnued to increase this week, and the market esƟmates a further signiﬁcant decline in pig iron output, puƫng pressure on iron ore prices. In the short term, iron ore prices lack upward momentum and are expected to conƟnue a weak and volaƟle trend.
